title: Implement anomaly scoring pipeline for structured-output regressions tied to model/config diffs
creator: Nora Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, schema-aware anomaly scoring pipeline that detects quality regressions in structured JSON outputs (field-level and record-level) and correlates alerts with recent model or config changes (model version, quantization profile, batching config, routing policy).

Motivation: We currently surface broad evaluation regressions from batch evals but lack a continuous, per-field signal that ties regressions to recent deploy deltas. This ticket reduces MTTD for structured-output regressions, enables early rollback for canaries, and powers targeted QA investigations.

Scope:
- Ingest streaming inference samples (canary and production samplers) and periodic golden-set replays.
- Parse produced JSON using schema definitions from the model contract repo. Support nested paths (e.g., items[2].price.amount).
- Compute per-field baseline statistics (type adherence rate, null-rate, distribution summaries for enums and numerics, token-length stats for strings).
- Compute per-field anomaly scores comparing target window (last X hours or canary window) vs baseline using robust measures (JS divergence, median absolute deviation, categorical KL with smoothing).
- Attribute anomalies to recent config/model diffs by correlating timestamped deploy metadata (model-version, quantize-profile, batch-policy) and running an attribution scoring heuristic (lift * confidence).
- Emit compact alert payloads to Console and to our Ops Slack channel with suggested rollback candidate (e.g., previous model variant) and actionable links.
- Store per-field time series and anomalies in the metrics store for dashboarding and postmortem analysis.

Non-goals: automated rollback, full ML-based root-cause inference (we will use heuristics first), heavy-weight on-device feature extraction for every token.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Schema coupling: We will rely on the existing model-contract YAMLs. To avoid brittle failures we fall back to permissive parsing and surface "schema-unknown" anomalies separately.
- Windowing: initial default windows = baseline last 14 days, target last 1h for canary and 24h for production bursts. These are configurable per-project.
- Thresholding: use adaptive thresholds calibrated by field volatility percentiles rather than fixed absolute thresholds. This reduces noisy alerts on high-variance fields.
- Performance: compute per-field lightweight summaries in streaming fashion (count, nulls, hist sketches) to limit storage and CPU cost.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Pipeline ingests sample stream and produces per-field anomaly scores for synthetic golden outputs (verified on the sample dataset).
2) Alert payloads include: affected fields, anomaly score, baseline metric snapshot, top correlated deploy/change (model or config), and links to failing examples.
3) New Console dashboard visualizes top anomalous fields, time series of metric deltas, and recent deploys for correlation.
4) End-to-end latency from sample ingestion to alert <= 10 minutes for canary pipeline.
5) False positive rate on labeled historical regressions <= 15% using held-out backtest set.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (dev): prototype on sample dataset and golden-set replay (2 weeks).
- Phase 2 (canary): deploy to canary stream for 3 internal teams; tune thresholds and attribution (2 weeks).
- Phase 3 (prod opt-in): expose as opt-in monitor in Console; enable for top 10 customers via Dedicated rollout (4 weeks).

Metrics to monitor:
- Precision/recall on historical labeled regressions (daily backtest).
- Alerts per-week per-customer (noise rate).
- Mean time to detection (MTTD) and time to triage.
- Compute/ingest cost per million samples.

Integration points:
- Model metadata service for version/config tags.
- Console alerting and runbooks.
- Evals datastore for golden-set and replay capability.

Open questions:
- How to weight fields by business impact automatically? We propose initial manual weights in project config.
- Whether to include text similarity metrics for free-form string fields vs strict schema checks. Start with schema-first then iterate.

Longer-term: integrate with rollout engine to create automatic canary failure gates and tie into Optimize recommendations for quantization or batching if regressions are caused by config changes.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline calculates and stores per-field metrics for streamed and golden samples
Alerts include attribution to the most-likely model/config change and example traces
Console dashboard shows field-level deltas and recent deploys for correlation
Latency from sample to alert <= 10 minutes in canary mode
Backtested FPR <= 15% on historical labeled regressions
